single_cve.body:
CAUTION: External email. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Dear IS Stakeholder,

Kindly pay attention to the following advisory Security A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-58319, has been identified in Apache Doris, a high-performance real-time analytical database. The vulnerability is caused by improper authentication in the Frontend (FE) HTTP REST administrative API, allowing certain administrative endpoints to be accessed without authentication. An unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to the Frontend HTTP service could perform unauthorized administrative operations, potentially impacting cluster integrity, stability, and service availability. Successful exploitation could lead to disruption of database operations or denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.

TECHNICAL DETAILS
A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-58319, has been identified in Apache Doris, a high-
performance real-time analytical database. The vulnerability is caused by improper authentication in
the Frontend (FE) HTTP REST administrative API, allowing certain administrative endpoints to be
accessed without authentication. An unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to the
Frontend HTTP service could perform unauthorized administrative operations, potentially impacting
cluster integrity, stability, and service availability. Successful exploitation could lead to disruption of
database operations or denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.
Vulnerability Details:
• CVE-2026-58319 – Improper Authentication in Apache Doris Frontend HTTP API
• CVSS v3.1: 9.1 (Critical)
• The vulnerability is caused by improper authentication checks in the Apache Doris Frontend (FE)
HTTP REST administrative API.
• Certain administrative HTTP REST endpoints can be accessed without requiring valid
authentication credentials.
• A remote attacker with network connectivity to the FE HTTP service can send unauthorized
administrative requests.
• No authentication or user interaction is required to exploit the vulnerability.
• The vulnerability may lead to denial-of-service (DoS) conditions or other operational
disruptions.
• Apache Doris versions 2.1.0 through versions prior to 3.1.0 are affected.
• The issue has been resolved in Apache Doris version 3.1.0.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026550 Published on: 23-July-2026
RECOMMENDATIONS
• Update Apache Doris to fixed version 3.1.0 or later.
• Regularly audit your FE HTTP access logs to check for any unauthorized connection attempts or
administrative requests from unrecognized IP addresses.
• Use network firewalls, security groups, or reverse proxies to ensure the customized / default ports
(default Port 8030 for HTTP and 8036 for HTTPS) in use are only accessible from trusted internal IP
addresses or management VPCs.

products_table.subject: [EXTERNAL] Security Advisory :: DOH- 2026551 - MICROSOFT SHAREPOINT SERVER CRITICAL DESERIALIZATION REMOTE CODE EXECUTION
products_table.body:
CAUTION: External email. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Dear IS Stakeholder,

Kindly pay attention to the following advisory Security A critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-58644, in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server is under confirmed active exploitation. The flaw stems from deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) and carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8. Microsoft shipped the fix as part of the July 14, 2026 Patch Tuesday release without an initial exploitation flag; CISA subsequently confirmed in-the-wild abuse and added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on July 16, 2026, with a Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 remediation deadline of July 19, 2026, for FCEB agencies.Microsoft's own advisory describes the exploitation precondition as an attacker already authenticated with at least Site Owner privileges on the target site. Independent vulnerability research from Trend Micro's Zero-Day Initiative (ZDI) and Cisco Talos characterize this CVE - paired with the related bug CVE-2026-50522 - as reachable without authentication or user interaction. This is a genuine discrepancy in public reporting rather than a resolved fact; treat the vulnerability as exploitable by any party who can reach the SharePoint front end, and do not rely on the Site Owner precondition as a compensating control.CVE-2026-58644 was disclosed alongside a broader cluster of on-premises SharePoint flaws being actively abused together - CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, and CVE-2026-56164 - which CISA reports are being chained to steal IIS machine keys and establish persistent access following initial RCE. All supported on-premises editions (Subscription Edition, 2019, 2016) are affected. SharePoint Online is not impacted.

SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER
ADVISORY
MICROSOFT SHAREPOINT SERVER CRITICAL DESERIALIZATION
REMOTE CODE EXECUTION
Severity: Critical
+000 0 0000000| soc@example.invalid
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026551 Published on: 23-July-2026
OVERVIEW
A critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-58644, in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint
Server is under confirmed active exploitation. The flaw stems from deserialization of untrusted data
(CWE-502) and carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8. Microsoft shipped the fix as part of the July 14, 2026
Patch Tuesday release without an initial exploitation flag; CISA subsequently confirmed in-the-wild
abuse and added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on July 16, 2026, with a
Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 remediation deadline of July 19, 2026, for FCEB agencies.
Microsoft's own advisory describes the exploitation precondition as an attacker already authenticated
with at least Site Owner privileges on the target site. Independent vulnerability research from Trend
Micro's Zero-Day Initiative (ZDI) and Cisco Talos characterize this CVE - paired with the related bug CVE-
2026-50522 - as reachable without authentication or user interaction. This is a genuine discrepancy in
public reporting rather than a resolved fact; treat the vulnerability as exploitable by any party who can
reach the SharePoint front end, and do not rely on the Site Owner precondition as a compensating
control.CVE-2026-58644 was disclosed alongside a broader cluster of on-premises SharePoint flaws
being actively abused together - CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, and CVE-2026-56164 - which CISA
reports are being chained to steal IIS machine keys and establish persistent access following initial RCE.
All supported on-premises editions (Subscription Edition, 2019, 2016) are affected. SharePoint Online is
not impacted.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
CVE ID: CVE-2026-58644
Occurred / Disclosed: Published July 14, 2026 (Microsoft July Patch Tuesday); added to CISA KEV July
16, 2026
Severity: CRITICAL
CVSS Score: 9.8 (CVSS v3.1)
CWE Category: CWE-502 - Deserialization of Untrusted Data
Category: Remote Code Execution (RCE)
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026551 Published on: 23-July-2026
SharePoint fails to properly validate serialized objects submitted over the network before
reconstructing them into application objects. A specially crafted serialized payload sent to a vulnerable
endpoint causes the server to instantiate attacker-controlled objects during deserialization, resulting in
arbitrary code execution in the context of the SharePoint application pool. Microsoft rates attack
complexity as low, noting the exploit does not require deep prior knowledge of the target and can be
repeated reliably against unpatched instances.
ATTACK VECTOR
Attacker Profile:
Opportunistic and targeted actors alike, ranging from ransomware affiliates to APT groups; the reliability
of deserialization RCE against internet-facing collaboration platforms makes this attractive to both
smash-and-grab and long-dwell operators.
Target Sector: Any organization running on-premises SharePoint Server (Subscription Edition, 2019,
2016) exposed to the internet or reachable from a compromised internal segment. Government,
finance, healthcare, and education entities with document-heavy collaboration workflows are
disproportionately represented among deployments.
Post-Exploitation Activity: Consistent with the wider SharePoint exploitation wave CISA has flagged
(CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164), observed and expected follow-on behavior
includes theft of IIS/ASP.NET machine keys to forge authentication tokens and survive patching; web
shell deployment for persistence; lateral movement from the SharePoint farm toward Active Directory-
integrated services; and staging for ransomware or data exfiltration.
Attack Chain:
• Attackers obtain or compromise a SharePoint account (credential stuffing, phishing, or reuse)
that holds Site Owner permissions, or in the unauthenticated-reachable scenario described by
ZDI/Talos, reaches the vulnerable endpoint directly.
• Attacker fingerprints the target SharePoint farm to confirm it is running a build below the July
2026 fixed version.
• A crafted request containing a malicious serialized object is submitted to the vulnerable
SharePoint component.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026551 Published on: 23-July-2026
• The server deserializes the payload without adequate validation, instantiating attacker-
controlled code.
• Code executes in the SharePoint application pool context; attacker establishes a web shell or
scheduled task for persistence.
• Attacker harvests IIS machine keys and/or pivots toward domain-joined infrastructure for
lateral movement and further compromise.
AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND FIXES
Product Affected Versions Impacted Fixed Version / Patch Available
Component Patch
SharePoint Builds below Core KB5002891 (build Yes
Server 2016 16.0.5561.1001 deserialization 16.0.5561.1001)
handling
SharePoint Builds below Core KB5002883 (build Yes
Server 2019 16.0.10417.20175 deserialization 16.0.10417.20175)
handling
SharePoint Builds below Core KB5002882 (build Yes
Server 16.0.19725.20434 deserialization 16.0.19725.20434)
Subscription handling
Edition
SharePoint Not affected N/A N/A - Microsoft- Yes
Online managed
RECOMMENDATIONS
• Review and restrict Site Owner and high-privilege SharePoint role assignments to reduce potential
access vectors.
• Minimize direct internet exposure for on-premises SharePoint servers; use a reverse proxy or Web
Application Firewall (WAF) to filter anomalous requests.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026551 Published on: 23-July-2026
• Rotate IIS/ASP.NET machine keys after patching and completing threat-hunting activities, as a
precaution against persistence mechanisms.
REFERENCES:
• https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
PLEASE NOTE
• Ensure all changes to the organization’s environment shall be conducted in a controlled manner and
aligned with the established Change Management process.
• Please test all patches and IOC in an UAT environment before deploying to production to avoid any
service disruptions.

SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER
ADVISORY
Active Exploitation of CheckPoint Critical Flaw (CVE-2026-16232)
Severity: Critical
+000 0 0000000| soc@example.invalid
Advisory Number: DOH-2026558 Published on: 26-Jul-2026
OVERVIEW
This advisory is about CheckPoint addressed a critical vulnerability affecting its Security
Management and Multi-Domain Security Management products. The flaw tracked as CVE-2026-
16232 (CVSS: 9.1) – ‘Improper Authentication’ vulnerability in the CheckPoint SmartConsole login
process using an application token, could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an
application login token and authenticate with full administrative privileges under specific
conditions.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
Successful exploitation of the vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to
obtain an application login token, authenticate with full administrative privileges, and modify
security policies and security configurations. Remote exploitation requires internet access to the
Management Server IP address and a configuration that does not restrict Trusted Clients.
AFFECTED PRODUCT & VERSIONS:
Check Point Security Management and Check Point Multi-Domain Security Management [MDS]
versions R77.30, R80, R80.10, R80.20, R80.30, R81 R81.10, R81.20, R82, R82.10
Compromise of a Security Management Server is particularly consequential because it sits at the
top of the trust hierarchy. An attacker with administrative access can modify security policies
across managed gateways, alter administrator permissions, manipulate VPN configurations, and
potentially disable or tamper with logging and monitoring. According to Check Point's advisory, the
vulnerabilities were discovered during a routine internal review, with subsequent analysis
revealing that CVE-2026-16232 had been exploited prior to the availability of a patch.
Check Point network security products have been targeted by multiple in-the-wild vulnerabilities
over the past two years. In June 2026, CVE-2026-50751, a critical authentication bypass in Check
Point Remote Access VPN, was exploited in the wild and added to the CISA KEV. In May 2024, CVE-
2024-24919, a high-severity information disclosure vulnerability in Check Point Quantum Security
Advisory Number: DOH-2026558 Published on: 26-Jul-2026
Gateways, was also exploited in the wild. Organizations running affected Check Point management
products should apply the available hotfixes on an emergency basis.
RECOMMENDATIONS
CheckPoint has released the patch to mitigate vulnerability and strongly recommends all admins
to upgrade to the latest versions. CheckPoint has shared mitigation steps:
• Follow the Check Point Hardening Best Practices Guide.
• Limit Trusted Clients (GUI clients) to trusted IP addresses/subnets. To do so:
o In SmartConsole, go to Manage & Settings > Permissions & Administrators > Trusted
Clients. Double-click the client you want to edit.
o In the Trusted Client configuration window that opens, change the settings as needed and.
Make sure do not use "Any" as a Type.
o Click OK.
• Protect Management access with Firewall, restrict access to tusted IP addresses, and verify
that implied rules for control connections are enabled. This will create an implied rule that will
prevent management access for non authorized IP addresses.
REFERENCES
• https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk185169/
PLEASE NOTE
• Ensure all changes to the organization’s environment shall be conducted in a controlled
manner and aligned with the established Change Management process.
• Please test all patches and IOC in an UAT environment before deploying to production to avoid
any service disruptions.
Advisory Number: DOH-2026558 Published on: 26-Jul-2026

OVERVIEW
A Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploit has been publicly released for CVE-2026-31694, a high-severity local privilege
escalation vulnerability affecting the Linux Kernel Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) subsystem. The vulnerability
allows an unprivileged local attacker to exploit flaws within the FUSE implementation to obtain root privileges

The public availability of exploit code significantly increases the likelihood of weaponization by threat actors,
enabling attackers with local access to compromise Linux servers, cloud workloads, container hosts, and
enterprise endpoints. Organizations utilizing Linux systems with FUSE enabled should prioritize remediation
and implement appropriate security controls to reduce the risk of privilege escalation attacks.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
CVE: CVE-2026-31694
Severity: High
CVSS: 7.8
Vulnerability Type: Local Privilege Escalation
Description:
CVE-2026-31694 is a local privilege escalation vulnerability affecting the Linux Kernel's Filesystem in Userspace
(FUSE) subsystem. The flaw allows an unprivileged local user to exploit weaknesses in the FUSE implementation
to elevate privileges and obtain root-level access.
The vulnerability affects the security boundary between user space and kernel space. Successful exploitation
enables attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges, resulting in complete system
compromise.
A publicly available Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploit has been released, lowering the barrier for exploitation and
increasing the risk of malicious use by threat actors.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026562 Published on: 29-July-2026
Impact
• Successful exploitation may allow attackers to:
• Escalate privileges from an unprivileged user to root
• Execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges.
• Disable or bypass security controls.
• Establish persistence on compromised systems.
• Conduct lateral movement within enterprise environments.
• Access, modify, or destroy sensitive data.
• Deploy additional malware or ransomware.
AFFECTED PRODUCTS
Platform Affected Versions Fixed Versions
Linux Kernel (FUSE Vulnerable kernel versions Refer to your Linux
Subsystem) utilizing the FUSE subsystem distribution vendors
Note: The vulnerability may affect multiple Linux distributions that ship vulnerable Linux Kernel versions
with the FUSE subsystem enabled.
RECOMMENDATIONS
• Upgrade affected Linux systems to vendor-provided kernel versions containing fixes for CVE-2026-31694
as soon as updates become available.
• Restrict or disable FUSE functionality where operationally feasible and limit mount permissions to trusted
users only.
• Enforce the principle of least privilege by minimizing local user permissions and restricting unnecessary
shell access.
• Enable Linux kernel security mechanisms such as KASLR, SMEP, SMAP, and other supported hardening
features.
• Continuously monitor systems for privilege escalation attempts and suspicious kernel-level activity using
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026562 Published on: 29-July-2026
• Review and restrict privileged access mechanisms including sudo, setuid, and setgid binaries.
• Ensure container hosts are updated with patched kernel versions and implement container runtime
security controls.
• Perform regular vulnerability assessments to identify Linux systems running vulnerable kernel versions.
• Monitor vendor security advisories for updated remediation guidance and apply security updates
through established change management processes.

SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER
ADVISORY
Memory-Resident OctLurk and SilkLurk Backdoors Deployed Against
Government Organizations
Severity: High
+000 0 0000000| soc@example.invalid
Advisory Number: DOH - 2026585 Published on: 04- Aug-2026
OVERVIEW
On 30 July 2026, researchers uncovered two previously unidentified backdoors, OctLurk and SilkLurk,
being used in a cyber-espionage campaign targeting organizations primarily across Central Asia since
January 2025. The activity affected government entities and organizations in sectors including
healthcare, research, foreign affairs, logistics, law enforcement, urban planning, facilities
management, and education. Researchers determined that both malware families are heavily
obfuscated, customized for specific victims, and capable of loading additional modules to conduct
command execution, file operations, credential theft, network scanning, keylogging, email collection,
and remote access activities. The investigation also identified the deployment of a supporting utility
known as LurkProxy, with evidence suggesting a common threat actor operates both malware families.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
Considering the strategic importance of government institutions, public-sector organizations, and
critical services within the UAE, the techniques demonstrated in this campaign highlight the threat
posed by highly tailored espionage malware designed for long-term covert access. The use of victim-
specific loaders, memory-resident malware, credential harvesting, remote administration capabilities,
and extensive post-compromise tooling could affect organizations handling sensitive government,
diplomatic, operational, or research-related information. The Cyber Threat Intelligence Team strongly
advises organizations to adhere to the recommendations and indicators outlined in this advisory to
effectively mitigate the risks posed by this threat.
The campaign centers on the deployment of the OctLurk and SilkLurk backdoors, which researchers
observed targeting organizations across Central Asia. Both malware families utilize customized loaders
that rely on system-specific information from victim machines to decrypt malicious payloads, making
them difficult to analyse and detect. The backdoors are heavily obfuscated and primarily operate in
memory. Researchers noted that the same threat actor likely operates both malware families, with
some victims hosting both implants simultaneously. In addition to maintaining remote access, the
malware supports modular functionality through additional plugins capable of command shell access,
Advisory Number: DOH - 2026585 Published on: 04- Aug-2026
file management, user interaction simulation, credential theft, keylogging, browser password
extraction, email collection, network reconnaissance, and remote administration.
ATTACK CHAIN OVERVIEW:
The attack chain involved the use of administrative credentials to remotely create scheduled tasks and
malicious services that executed loader components. The loaders decrypted and decompressed
embedded payloads using a multi-stage process involving hard-coded keys and victim-specific system
information before reflectively injecting the backdoor directly into memory. Once loaded, the backdoor
collected host information including operating system details, computer and user information, network-
related information, and system time data. The collected information was compressed, encrypted
through multiple stages, and transmitted to the attackers. Commands and plugins received from
command-and-control infrastructure were decrypted, decompressed, and executed in memory,
allowing the threat actors to expand capabilities without relying on traditional on-disk payloads.
Further analysis showed that OctLurk supports a broad range of espionage-focused capabilities through
plugins. The file management component can enumerate drives, search for files, recursively collect file
metadata, create and modify files and directories, perform file transfers, and manipulate timestamps.
The command shell plugin enables interactive command execution and collection of command output.
The interaction management component supports screen capture, clipboard access, keyboard and
mouse simulation, and other user interaction functions. Researchers also reported that post-
compromise tooling associated with the campaign included credential dumping, browser password
theft, keylogging, network scanning, email harvesting, remote access utilities, and additional malware
deployment. The use of customized victim-specific loaders, reflective loading, layered encryption,
compression, and memory-resident execution demonstrates a strong emphasis on stealth and
operational security.
The research concludes that OctLurk and SilkLurk represent a focused espionage toolset designed for
stealth, persistence, and post-compromise collection in sensitive environments. Organizations should
prioritize detection of abnormal administrative activity, service-based execution, in-memory payload
behavior, credential access attempts, and unusual plugin-driven post-exploitation activity.

ADVISORY

Severity: Critical

Advisory Number: DOH-2026516 Published on: 11-July-2026
OVERVIEW
This advisory addresses an unverified claim regarding a Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability
affecting Microsoft SharePoint Server, tracked as CVE-2026-33112.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
CVE-2026-33112 is a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting on-premises Microsoft
SharePoint Server, rooted in insecure deserialization (CWE-502) of untrusted .NET DataSet objects. The
flaw was addressed by Microsoft as part of the May 2026 Patch Tuesday release. A public proof-of-
concept (PoC) was disclosed on July 7, 2026 by Viettel Security, demonstrating a working bypass of the
XmlValidator safe-control mechanism that Microsoft had introduced to remediate the earlier CVE-2025-
53770 SharePoint ToolShell chain. The bypass allows any low-privilege, authenticated SharePoint site
member to achieve arbitrary code execution in the context of the SharePoint application pool
(w3wp.exe), with no user interaction required.
CVE ID: CVE-2026-33112
Occurred: Disclosed/patched by Microsoft on May 12, 2026; public RCE PoC released July 7, 2026
Severity: High / Critical
CVSS Score: 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Category: Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) leading to Remote Code Execution
Description:
SharePoint Server's PerformancePoint Services component builds an XSD schema set when processing
DataSet objects submitted to the BIMonitoringAuthoringService web service. The vulnerable code path
resolves external schema references declared via <xsd:import> and <xsd:include> elements over the
network rather than validating them locally. Because the referenced schema is fetched from an attacker-
controlled host at request time, the XmlValidator safe-control introduced by Microsoft's second CVE-
202553770 fix (the TypeNameParserImpl generic-type check) never inspects the resulting type
definitions, effectively blinding the validation logic. The PPSAuthoringService.asmx TestConnection
method indirectly invokes ExcelDataSet.get_DataTable() during connection testing, triggering
Advisory Number: DOH-2026516 Published on: 11-July-2026
deserialization of the attacker-supplied gadget chain and resulting in code execution under the
SharePoint application pool identity.
ATTACK VECTOR
Attacker Profile: Authenticated attacker holding any low-privilege SharePoint account (e.g., standard site
member); no elevated privileges or user interaction required
Target Sector: Organizations running on-premises SharePoint Server (Subscription Edition, 2019, 2016
Enterprise) government, education, and enterprise environments with internetfacing or internally
exposed SharePoint farms
Post-Exploitation Activity:
• Attacker authenticates to the target SharePoint site with a valid low-privilege account and
creates a SharePoint list item to use as a deserialization anchor.
• Attackers stand up an external HTTP server hosting a malicious XSD schema reachable from the
SharePoint server.
• A crafted request is submitted to /_vti_bin/PPS/PPSAuthoringService.asmx (TestConnection),
referencing the list item via the ItemUrl parameter and importing the attacker-hosted schema.
• SharePoint resolves the external schema, bypassing XmlValidator, and deserializes the
embedded gadget chain via ExcelDataSet.get_DataTable(), leading to arbitrary command
execution under w3wp.exe.
• Observed proof-of-concept behavior includes spawning of child processes (e.g., calc.exe in
testing) confirming code execution; in live attacks these maps to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or
rundll32.exe as follow-on payload droppers.

EXPLOITATION STATUS
As of this advisory, Microsoft and NVD/EPSS scoring (as of May 17, 2026) had not flagged CVE-2026-
33112 as known exploited in the wild. However, a fully weaponized public PoC - including exact
reproduction steps, the vulnerable endpoint, and payload trigger method - was published by Viettel
Security and covered widely on July 7, 2026. Given the low privilege bar, lack of required user interaction,
and full public disclosure of the exploitation chain, the likelihood of in-the-wild exploitation should now
be treated as high. This CVE should be reprioritized as actively exploitable pending confirmation of
exploitation telemetry.
Advisory Number: DOH-2026516 Published on: 11-July-2026
RECOMMENDATIONS
• Apply the May 2026 Microsoft Security Update for the applicable SharePoint edition (Subscription
Edition, 2019, or 2016 Enterprise) immediately across all farm roles - web front-end, application, and
search servers.
• Inventory all SharePoint farms in the environment and confirm patch/build-number deployment
against the Microsoft Update Catalog entry for CVE-2026-33112.
• Restrict or monitor access to /_vti_bin/PPS/PPSAuthoringService.asmx; disable PerformancePoint
Services where not actively used to eliminate the exposed attack surface.
• Monitor and, where feasible, restrict outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from SharePoint servers to
unfamiliar external hosts, particularly around SOAP requests to PPSAuthoringService.asmx.
• Hunt for anomalous TestConnection calls, unexpected child processes spawned by w3wp.exe
(cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe), and .NET Runtime errors referencing BinaryFormatter,
LosFormatter, or ObjectStateFormatter in Windows Event Logs and SharePoint ULS logs.
• Deploy WAF/reverse-proxy signatures to detect serialized .NET payload patterns and known
ysoserial.net gadget chain signatures (e.g., TypeConfuseDelegate, ActivitySurrogateSelector) in
inbound SharePoint requests.
• Run SharePoint application pools under least-privilege service accounts to constrain blast radius if
exploitation occurs, and rotate farm/service account credentials if compromise is suspected.
• Enforce MFA on all SharePoint accounts to reduce risk from credential-based access to the
authenticated entry point this vulnerability requires.

OVERVIEW
Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM WebSphere Application Server that could allow unauthenticated
attackers to execute arbitrary code, gain elevated privileges, access sensitive information, or perform
server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
Vulnerability Details
• CVE-2026-14512 Severity: Critical | CVSS: 9.8 An unsafe deserialization vulnerability that could
allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication or execute arbitrary code.
• CVE-2026-14446 Severity: Critical | CVSS: 9.8 An improper authentication vulnerability in the
administrative console that could allow an attacker to gain elevated privileges.
• CVE-2026-14529 Severity: High | CVSS: 9.4 A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
affecting environments where the SIP container feature is enabled. Successful exploitation
could allow an unauthenticated attacker to send crafted requests to internal systems.
• CVE-2026-14528 Severity: High | CVSS: 7.4 A sensitive information exposure vulnerability that
could allow confidential information to be disclosed through log files.
Affected Products and Versions
• IBM WebSphere Application Server 9.0
• IBM WebSphere Application Server 8.5
• IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty — Versions 192.0.2.1 through 192.0.2.1
Fixed Versions
Apply the relevant IBM interim fixes or update to the applicable fixed versions when available.

SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER
ADVISORY
Dysphoria Expands IoT Botnet into Large-Scale DDoS and Residential
Relay Network
Severity: High
+000 0 0000000| soc@example.invalid
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026638 Published on: 17-Aug-2026
OVERVIEW
Dysphoria is a rapidly expanding IoT botnet targeting internet-exposed routers, gateways, IP cameras,
DVRs, and other embedded Linux devices. The botnet has reportedly reached approximately 296,000
compromised devices and has evolved beyond DDoS attacks to include residential relay/proxy
capabilities. Dysphoria also uses Ethereum Name Service (ENS) and Solana Name Service (SNS) records
for resilient command-and-control (C2) infrastructure.
TECHNICAL DETAILS
Dysphoria is associated with the jackskid/fbot malware lineage and has undergone rapid development
since early 2026. Its primary targets include internet-facing embedded devices with exposed
management services, outdated firmware, weak credentials, and insecure configurations.
The malware supports multiple operational roles, including:
• Large-scale DDoS activity using compromised IoT devices.
• Relay/proxy functionality that allows attacker traffic to traverse compromised residential and
small-business networks.
• Blockchain-based infrastructure discovery through ENS and SNS records.
• Router configuration manipulation, including the use of port-mapping functionality to enable
inbound connectivity.
C2 Domains
dysphoria-c2.eth
dysphoria-net.eth
dysphoria-bot.sol
dysphoria-control.sol
iot-dysphoria.eth
SHA-256
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026638 Published on: 17-Aug-2026
Technical Impact:
• DDoS: Compromised devices can be used to generate large-scale distributed denial-of-service
traffic.
• Residential Proxy Abuse: Infected routers and gateways can become intermediary nodes,
causing malicious activity to appear to originate from legitimate residential or business IP
addresses.
• Network Exposure: Unauthorized port forwarding or UPnP changes may expose internal
services to the Internet.
• C2 Resilience: Blockchain-based naming infrastructure can make traditional domain-based C2
disruption more difficult.
• Reputation Risk: Public IP addresses associated with infected devices may become linked to
scanning, abuse, fraud, or other malicious activity.
• Lateral Movement: Compromised IoT devices connected to enterprise networks may provide
an additional pathway toward internal resources when network segmentation is insufficient.
• Limited Visibility: Embedded devices often have limited logging and may not be covered by
conventional EDR or endpoint security solutions.
RECOMMENDATIONS
• Identify and inventory all Internet-facing IoT devices, including routers, gateways, IP cameras,
DVRs, and embedded Linux systems.
• Apply the latest vendor firmware and security patches, and replace unsupported or end-of-life
devices.
• Disable unnecessary Telnet, SSH, UPnP, and public-facing remote-management services.
• Change default or weak administrative credentials to strong, unique passwords and enable MFA
where supported.
• Review NAT, port-forwarding, and router configurations for unauthorized changes and suspicious
inbound or outbound traffic.
Advisory Number: DOH- 2026638 Published on: 17-Aug-2026
• Isolate IoT devices through network segmentation and continuously monitor them for abnormal
traffic, DDoS activity, and suspicious C2 communications.
REFERENCES
:
• https://cyberpress.org/dysphoria-botnet-hijacks-iot/
PLEASE NOTE
• Ensure all changes to the organization’s environment shall be conducted in a controlled manner and
aligned with the established Change Management process.
• Please test all patches and IOC in an UAT environment before deploying to production to avoid any
service disruptions.
ACTION
• Kindly provide us with your feedback base on our recommendations.
• Report any incidents detected relating to this advisory.
